skill.name: scientific-writing
skill.description: Guides scientific manuscript drafting, revision, citation formatting, figure planning, and reporting guideline checks for research papers and journal submissions.
skill.summary: Draft and revise scientific manuscripts with IMRAD structure, citations, figures, and reporting guidelines.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The audit found mostly documentation-only false positives from citation examples, Markdown fences, and scientific writing guidance. One medium-risk Bash example remains confirmed because it encourages running a local Python script that is not included in the reviewed skill. I also found a medium semantic privacy risk from mandatory external schematic generation without explicit user consent.

remediation.issue: Bash example executes an unreviewed local schematic script.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the Bash command or require explicit user approval after verifying the script path, arguments, and source. Prefer non-executable guidance when possible.

remediation.issue: Mandatory external AI schematic generation can expose unpublished research content.
remediation.suggestion: Make external figure generation optional, disclose the external service, and ask for user consent before sending manuscript details outside the workspace.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory External Schematic Generation Without Consent
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md requires every paper to include AI-generated figures and says Nano Banana Pro will generate and refine schematics. This can route unpublished manuscript ideas or research details to an external service without an explicit user consent step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly makes external AI figure generation mandatory and names a third-party generator. The package does not describe a consent gate or data handling limits, so the privacy risk is credible but depends on how the referenced skill is installed.

content.value_statement: Scientific papers need clear structure, precise language, and correct reporting details. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft polished manuscripts with citations, figures, and guideline checks.
actual_capabilities: Drafts and revises manuscript sections using IMRAD structure.
Converts research outlines into full scientific prose.
Applies APA, AMA, Vancouver, Chicago, and IEEE citation guidance.
Plans figures and tables with captions, labels, and accessibility checks.
Checks reporting requirements for CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, and related standards.
Adapts terminology for biomedical, engineering, ecology, psychology, and other fields.
limitations: It does not verify citations unless paired with a research lookup workflow.
It cannot replace journal author instructions or expert peer review.
It may require user-supplied study details, data, and target journal requirements.
External schematic generation should be used only with user consent.

use_cases.title: Draft a First Manuscript
use_cases.description: Turn study notes, results, and references into a structured IMRAD draft with complete paragraphs.

use_cases.title: Prepare Journal Submission Text
use_cases.description: Align citations, tables, figures, and required statements with a target journal format.

use_cases.title: Improve Clarity Before Review
use_cases.description: Revise dense sections for precision, logical flow, consistent terminology, and measured claims.

prompt_templates.title: Create an IMRAD Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an IMRAD outline for my study. Use my objective, methods, main findings, and target journal to organize the paper.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Methods Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft the Methods section in full paragraphs. Include study design, participants, procedures, measurements, ethics, and statistical analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Revise for Journal Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise this manuscript section for the target journal. Improve clarity, terminology, citation style, figure references, and word count.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Reporting Completeness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this manuscript against the correct reporting guideline. Identify missing items and suggest exact revisions for each section.

output_examples.input: Study notes for a randomized trial need an Introduction section.
output_examples.output: A full-paragraph Introduction that establishes context, identifies the evidence gap, cites key prior work, and states the study objective.

output_examples.input: A Results section repeats every value from Table 1.
output_examples.output: A concise Results paragraph that highlights the main pattern, references Table 1, and avoids duplicating all table data.

output_examples.input: A systematic review draft needs PRISMA readiness checks.
output_examples.output: A checklist-style review of missing eligibility criteria, search strategy details, selection process, data extraction, and bias assessment text.

best_practices: Provide the target journal, study type, and reporting guideline before drafting.
Use outlines for planning, then convert them into complete paragraphs.
Verify citations, statistics, and claims against the original sources.
anti_patterns: Do not leave planning bullet points in final manuscript sections.
Do not overstate findings beyond the study design and data.
Do not send unpublished research to external tools without consent.

faq.question: Can this skill write a complete paper?
faq.answer: Yes, it can draft complete manuscript sections when you provide study details, results, references, and journal requirements.

faq.question: Does it verify every citation?
faq.answer: No. Use a research lookup workflow or manual checks to confirm source accuracy and citation details.

faq.question: Which citation styles are covered?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for APA, AMA, Vancouver, Chicago, and IEEE styles.

faq.question: Can it handle reporting guidelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, STARD, TRIPOD, ARRIVE, CARE, SQUIRE, SPIRIT, and CHEERS guidance.

faq.question: Is external figure generation required?
faq.answer: The source skill strongly requires schematics, but users should confirm before sending unpublished details to external tools.

faq.question: Is this a substitute for expert review?
faq.answer: No. Domain experts should review methods, statistics, interpretations, and compliance with journal policies.
